title: FWSpoof - Recreated Network Attack Prevention Tool
instructions: Recreate the fwspoof program from scratch with a clean, modular architecture. The program analyzes tcpdump packet captures to detect and block SYN flood and SYN+RESET spoofing attacks on HTTP servers. The new version should have clear separation of concerns, proper error handling, configuration management, and comprehensive logging.

1783934668.3802087.instruction:
Create a clean project structure with the following directories and files:
- fwspoof/ (main package directory)
  - __init__.py
  - config.py (configuration management)
  - parser.py (packet parsing)
  - detector.py (attack detection logic)
  - blocker.py (iptables integration)
  - stats.py (statistics collection)
  - logger.py (logging utilities)
- tests/ (test directory)
  - __init__.py
  - test_parser.py
  - test_detector.py
- main.py (entry point)
- requirements.txt
- config.yaml (default configuration)

Ensure proper Python package structure with __init__.py files. The structure should follow modern Python best practices with clear separation of concerns.

log.text: Created complete project structure with fwspoof package directory containing config.py, parser.py, detector.py, blocker.py, stats.py, logger.py modules; tests directory with test_parser.py and test_detector.py; main.py entry point; requirements.txt with PyYAML dependency; config.yaml default configuration file; and proper __init__.py files for Python package structure.

1783934668.3803837.instruction:
Create fwspoof/config.py that handles all configuration settings. Include:
- Default configuration values (max_flag_count=20, max_flag_count_per_cidr=3, etc.)
- YAML configuration file loading
- Environment variable support
- Configuration validation
- Type hints for all settings

The config should manage: thresholds for SYN attacks, thresholds for SYN+RESET attacks, connection type (INPUT/FORWARD/OUTPUT), allowed IPs list, flags to monitor ([S], [R]), verbose mode, test mode, and specific IP blocking mode.

log.text: Enhanced fwspoof/config.py with complete configuration management including: environment variable support (FWSPOOF_ prefix), configuration validation with ConfigValidationError, Config.load() method for multi-source configuration (env vars > YAML > defaults), type hints throughout, allowed_ips file loading with count return, to_dict() and __str__ methods for debugging, and init_config() helper function.

1783934668.3816295.instruction:
Create fwspoof/parser.py that parses tcpdump output lines. The module should:
- Parse timestamp, source IP, destination IP, and TCP flags from each line
- Extract first two octets (fto), first three octets (ftt), and full IP
- Handle various tcpdump output formats
- Return structured data objects (dataclasses) for parsed packets
- Include error handling for malformed lines
- Add type hints throughout

Create a Packet dataclass with fields: timestamp, source_ip, dest_ip, flags, fto, ftt, sip.

log.text: Enhanced fwspoof/parser.py with: TCPFlag enum for type-safe flag handling, frozen Packet dataclass with optional fields (sport, dip, dport), robust timestamp parsing with validation, IP validation, regex-based parsing with fallback, calculate_octets() helper, parse_lines() batch processing, get_packet_summary() for debugging, comprehensive error handling, and full type hints with detailed docstrings.

1783934668.3818383.instruction:
Create fwspoof/detector.py that analyzes parsed packets for attack patterns. The module should:
- Track packet counts per IP range (fto/ftt levels)
- Detect SYN flood attacks (repeated [S] flags)
- Detect SYN+RESET attacks (alternating [S] and [R] flags)
- Maintain in-memory state of suspicious activity
- Implement configurable thresholds for blocking decisions
- Support both range-based and specific IP blocking
- Return detection results with metadata (which IPs/ranges to block)

Use dictionaries with proper keys (crc32b hashes or tuples) for efficient lookups. Include methods to check if an IP/range should be blocked.

log.text: Enhanced fwspoof/detector.py with: three-level tracking (RangeStats, SubnetStats, IPStats), SYN+RESET pattern detection with _is_syn_reset_pattern and _update_syn_reset_count methods, configurable thresholds for global and per-CIDR attacks, specific IP blocking support via check_specific_ip_attack, AttackResult dataclass for structured results, blocked IP tracking, comprehensive statistics with get_stats and get_range_info, proper CRC32 hashing for all keys, and full type hints with detailed docstrings.

1783934668.38204.instruction:
Create fwspoof/blocker.py that handles iptables integration. The module should:
- Load currently blocked IPs from iptables
- Block IP ranges (/24 CIDR) using iptables
- Unblock IP ranges when attacks stop
- Support test mode (no actual iptables commands)
- Support specific IP blocking vs range blocking
- Track blocked state in memory to avoid duplicate commands
- Include proper error handling for iptables failures

Functions needed: load_blocks(), block_ip(cidr_or_ip), unblock_ip(cidr_or_ip), is_blocked(cidr_or_ip).

log.text: Created fwspoof/blocker.py with: load_blocks() to load existing iptables rules, block_ip()/unblock_ip() universal methods for both ranges and specific IPs, is_blocked() for checking block status, BlockedEntry dataclass with hit_count tracking, BlockType enum, test mode support, proper error handling with try/except blocks, CRC32 hashing for keys, and helper methods for statistics.

1783934668.3821535.instruction:
Create fwspoof/stats.py and fwspoof/logger.py:
- stats.py: Track and report statistics (total packets, unique IPs, blocked, unblocked, etc.)
- logger.py: Centralized logging with verbose/debug modes, timestamped output

The stats module should collect: all packets processed, unique source IPs, single IP blocks, range blocks, unblock operations, already blocked count. Include a method to print summary statistics at exit.

The logger should support verbose mode, prefix messages, and integrate with Python's logging module.

log.text: Created fwspoof/stats.py with Statistics dataclass tracking packets, unique IPs, blocks, unblocks, timing, packets by flag, and top attackers. Includes print_summary() for formatted output and convenience functions. Created fwspoof/logger.py with Python logging integration, colored output, setup_logging(), log levels (debug, verbose, info, warning, error), and specialized functions like log_packet(), log_attack(), log_block().

1783934668.3822627.instruction:
Create main.py as the entry point with argparse-based CLI:
- --help, --version flags
- --max-flag-count (-M): Global threshold
- --max-flag-count-per-cidr (-m): Per-range SYN threshold  
- --max-flag-count-per-cidr-sr (-r): Per-range SYN+RESET threshold
- --verbose (-V): Debug output
- --stats (-S): Show statistics at exit
- --con-type (-C): INPUT/FORWARD/OUTPUT
- --dont-unblock (-D): Don't auto-unblock
- --test (-T): Test mode (no iptables)
- --specific-ip (-s): Block specific IPs instead of ranges

Wire all modules together: read from stdin, parse packets, detect attacks, manage blocking, output statistics.

log.text: Verified main.py is complete with all required CLI arguments using argparse, including all threshold options, behavior flags, and configuration file support. Main loop reads from stdin, parses packets, detects attacks, manages blocking, and outputs statistics. Cleanup handler registered for graceful shutdown.

1783934668.3823726.instruction:
Create tests for the core functionality:
- test_parser.py: Test parsing various tcpdump line formats, error handling
- test_detector.py: Test attack detection logic with synthetic data
- Include mock data for tcpdump lines
- Test threshold calculations and blocking decisions
- Test edge cases (empty input, malformed lines, boundary conditions)

Use Python's unittest framework. Create at least 5 test cases per module covering normal operation and edge cases.

log.text: Created comprehensive test suites for test_parser.py (14 test classes, 30+ test cases) and test_detector.py (9 test classes, 35+ test cases). Tests cover: timestamp parsing edge cases, IP extraction with multiple formats, TCP flag handling, SYN flood detection at various thresholds, SYN+RESET pattern detection, specific IP blocking, state management, boundary conditions, and error handling. Includes mock tcpdump data and synthetic packet generators.
